name: tier1_floor_review
_comment: THE FLOOR GATE SCENE — tier one, session one.
It is mixed_distribution.json plus the one context that spec could not supply, and the
reason it is a fourth spec rather than an edit is the reason already recorded on the third:
both existing specs are cited by evidence on disk, and swapping their geometry would
silently invalidate every comparison taken through them.
WHAT IT MUST CONTAIN, and this is not a preference — ART-BIBLE-v0 §8.2.1 states it as a
standing rule and then records that the rule was not met:
a floor candidate is not fully reviewed until it has been seen in at least: OPEN FLOOR,
THE CHANNEL, A TRODDEN CHOKEPOINT, and A NEGLECTED PASSAGE. A review scene shaped only
as narrow corridor cannot pose the §8.2 question.
... Those verdicts were rendered on a one-tile-wide corridor, where there is no centre
line distinct from the flanks. The paragraph above is the standing rule and IT WAS NOT
MET. A floor round that means to pose the §8.2 question must build the four-scene set
first; until it does, a wear cull is not fully chargeable to the tile.
So the four are built, and each one is here to be answered rather than to be present:
1. OPEN FLOOR. Room A, 7x6 at x5-11, y4-9. Wide enough that the trodden channel is
NARROWER THAN THE HALL, which is the whole of §8.2.1: 'a polished channel worn through
a wider hall ... ordinary floor flanks it'. A room the width of the channel cannot pose
that question any more than a one-wide corridor can.
2. THE CHANNEL. It runs room A -> chokepoint -> room B, because that is the map's longest
through-path and FloorIncidentPlanner derives the route as exactly that. §8.2.1: 'the
channel leads somewhere'.
3. A TRODDEN CHOKEPOINT. x=8, y10-15, one wide, ON the route: polished wall to wall,
'because the traffic had no room to spread'. §8.2.1 keeps the chokepoint in the game as
a load-bearing roguelike verb, so a floor set that cannot draw one is short a state.
4. A NEGLECTED PASSAGE — THE ONE mixed_distribution.json DOES NOT HAVE, and the reason
this file exists. A stub 2 wide at x2-3, y6-7, opening off room A's west wall through a
one-cell mouth at (4,7). It is a DEAD END, so no through-route can pass along it, and
the channel therefore does not reach it: §8.1's 'no traffic and no care -> decay'. Its
job is to be the negative half of §8.2 — 'polish means you are on the path, decay means
you have stepped off it' says nothing at all unless some floor in frame is off the path.
It is kept SHORT on purpose. The route is the graph diameter, and a long enough side
branch would become the diameter itself and get treaded — the neglected passage would
silently turn into the main route and the scene would stop containing the context it
was built for. Room A's far corner to room B's far corner is the longer pair, and the
engine logs the channel and neglected cell counts on every boot so the claim is checked
rather than asserted.
Room B sits at the bottom, outside the lit radius on purpose. The light arc (§6.2) is part
of the distribution too, and a scene where everything is lit is not the game. It matters
more here than it did for walls: §6.2.1's tuning pass is about legibility ACROSS the lit
radius rather than at its middle, so the scene has to have an outside.
THE PLAYER STANDS AT (8,6), INSIDE ROOM A, and the light is carried by the figure — so the
lit region moves as it is walked. The chokepoint mouth is 4 tiles away, the neglected
passage's mouth is 4, and room B is beyond the radius until you walk to it.
THE WALLS IN THIS SCENE ARE MOCKS and are not being judged. See
src/Presentation/assets/tier1_floors/tile_themes_tier1_floors.yaml for which tiles are real
art and which are the tier-0 programmer-art stubs, and for what that costs: §6.5's value
stack cannot be read against a stub wall, so this build answers the floor and rig questions
and does not answer the plane-relationship one.
_legibility: FLOOR SESSION TWO, PRECONDITION 2. The points this capture is REQUIRED to be able to show,
and the points it is required to leave dark. ProbeFloorLegibility refuses to write the PNG
if any of them fails.
It exists because ProbeJunctionLuminance guards a JUNCTION and this scene has none - it
reports junction=NO and that guard silently no-ops, so floor captures had no legibility
check of any kind. A scene whose subject had fallen outside the carried light would still
render, still pass determinism, and measure nothing.
DISTANCES ARE FROM THE PLAYER AT (8,6), and the ratified radius is 5.0 TILES (Ruling 56).
The outermost lit point is at FOUR tiles, not five, and that is a measured decision rather
than a convenient one. Swept at the ratified rig (tools/tier1_floors/sweep_legibility.py):
⚠ A POINT AT THE NOMINAL RADIUS READS THE SAME AS ONE DECLARED DARK. 0.060 against an
ambient floor of ~0.058. The lamp's DELIVERED reach at radius 5.0 is about four tiles; the
fifth is ambient. So (8,11) was withdrawn rather than declared either way - asserting it is
lit would fail every capture, and asserting it is dark would claim the scene wanted that.
THIS IS REPORTED, NOT TREATED AS A DEFECT IN RULING 56. The rig was ratified on the device
by eye and §13.2 makes the eye final; a luminance ratio has never been calibrated against
'legible to a person holding a phone in a dark room'. What the measurement supports is the
narrower claim that NOMINAL RADIUS AND DELIVERED REACH ARE DIFFERENT QUANTITIES, which is a
fact scene design needs and a question the next rig conversation owns.
THE DARK POINTS ARE NOT AN AFTERTHOUGHT. §6.2.1 rules the pass 'not a licence to flood the
Boundary with light' - you begin as the only thing here that burns is register and outranks
convenience. A guard that only asked 'is it bright enough' would green a drowned arc.
EVERY POINT IS INSIDE THE DUNGEON VIEW, which is a checked property and took two tries to
get right. The first dark points were (2,7) and (8,17): they land at x=-9 and y=1371 on a
750x1334 capture, PatchLuminance clips, and they were measuring the HUD and the letterbox -
0.059 and 0.160, one 'dark' point brighter than a 'lit' one, which is what exposed it. The
replacements at (8,15)/(8,16) were inside the IMAGE and still inside the HUD's button row,
reading 0.796 and getting DARKER as ambient rose. The dungeon view is (0,90)..(750,1001) -
the game's own UILayer/ViewportOverlay rect - and the probe now requires points inside it.
⚠ CONSEQUENCE WORTH RECORDING: at this camera, the visible band is about y 0-12, so ROOM B
(y16-18) IS NEVER IN A STATIC CAPTURE. It exists for the walked device review, not for the
headless one, and no still can be evidence about it.

legibility.why: room A north row, 2 tiles - open floor, the easy case
room A west flank, 3.2 tiles - ordinary floor beside the channel
room A east flank, 3.2 tiles - the mirror of the above
chokepoint mouth, 4 tiles - the trodden one-wide state
chokepoint, 6 tiles - past the ratified 5.0 radius, the arc's outside
the NEGLECTED passage, 5 tiles - off the route and off the light
